record.paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
record.original_question: How fast, and by what QCD dynamics, does a high-energy nuclear collision observable transition from the nonlinear saturation regime to the high-transverse-momentum leading-twist regime, given that current running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov small-x evolution equations do not include the DGLAP limit and predict that proton-nucleus nuclear-modification observables return to unity only at unrealistically large transverse momentum pT?

evidence.quote: How fast is the transition from the saturation regime to the high-pT (leading-twist) regime ? The most up-to-date non-linear QCD evolution equations, such as the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov (rcBK) equation, do not contain the DGLAP limit, hence after some evolution down in x (reflected in the data at forward rapidities), RpA predictions reach unity only at unrealistically large values of pT . This is an open question, to which p+A collisions at the LHC should have already provided some answers, once electron-nucleus (e+A) data become available.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider high-energy proton–nucleus (p+A) collisions in QCD. At small Bjorken x, gluon densities become large and the dynamics enter the nonlinear "saturation" regime, characterized by an emergent saturation scale Q_s(x) at which gluon recombination balances gluon emission. At large transverse momentum p_T ≫ Q_s, the dynamics is expected to reduce to collinear factorization with parton distributions evolving according to the linear DGLAP equations (the "leading-twist" regime). The current state-of-the-art nonlinear small-x evolution, the running-coupling Balitsky–Kovchegov (rcBK) equation, governs the unintegrated dipole amplitude N(x,r) and resums leading logarithms in 1/x with running-coupling corrections, but does not reduce to DGLAP evolution in the dilute/large-Q^2 limit. As a phenomenological consequence, the predicted nuclear modification factor

  R_{pA}(p_T, y) = (1/A) · [d^2 N^{pA}/dp_T dy] / [d^2 N^{pp}/dp_T dy]

computed using rcBK initial conditions and evolution approaches unity only at parametrically large p_T, beyond values currently considered physically realistic at forward rapidities.

Problem. Determine, within QCD, the rate and the underlying dynamical mechanism by which a small-x evolved nonlinear amplitude transitions to the leading-twist DGLAP regime as p_T increases above Q_s. Specifically:

1. Construct (or characterize) an evolution equation for the dipole amplitude N(x,r) that smoothly interpolates between rcBK behavior in the saturation/dilute-but-small-x region and DGLAP evolution of the collinear gluon distribution at large Q^2 = 1/r^2, and quantify how rapidly (in p_T at fixed x, or in x at fixed p_T) the leading-twist limit is recovered.

2. Using such a unified description, predict R_{pA}(p_T, y) for forward p+A collisions at LHC energies and identify the p_T scale at which R_{pA} → 1, demonstrating that this scale is realistic (i.e., reachable in current or near-future experiments) rather than parametrically large.

A satisfactory solution must specify the QCD dynamics responsible for the transition (e.g., the inclusion of the full DGLAP splitting kernel in the small-x evolution, higher-twist resummation, or matching/factorization between BK and DGLAP) and provide quantitative predictions for the transition rate that can be confronted with p+A and electron–nucleus data.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature shows ongoing efforts to bridge nonlinear small-x (BK/rcBK) evolution and DGLAP evolution via "DGLAP-improved" saturation models and matched evolution schemes, with comparisons to HERA and LHC p+A data delineating an applicability boundary rather than a fully unified equation. No single QCD framework has been established that both contains the DGLAP limit and quantitatively predicts the rate at which R_{pA} returns to unity at realistic p_T, so the question remains open with partial phenomenological progress.

status_evidence.title: Linear vs. non-linear QCD evolution: from HERA data to LHC phenomenology
status_evidence.snippet: rcBK non-linear evolution equations are compared with NNLO DGLAP fits to determine the kinematical region where rcBK accurately describes the data and its applicability boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary between rcBK and DGLAP regimes is still being mapped phenomenologically rather than unified.

status_evidence.title: Color dipole cross section in the DGLAP improved saturation model
status_evidence.snippet: DGLAP improved model significantly improves agreement at large Q^2 without affecting saturation physics at small Q^2.
status_evidence.claim: Hybrid DGLAP-improved saturation models exist as partial solutions but are not derived from a single nonlinear evolution equation containing the DGLAP limit.

status_evidence.title: Beyond DGLAP improved saturation model
status_evidence.snippet: Recent extensions continue to refine matching of saturation and DGLAP dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Active research as of 2023 indicates the unified description and transition rate are still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Pursuing the Precision Study for Color Glass Condensate
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses precision program for CGC including matching to collinear factorization and remaining open issues.
status_evidence.claim: Saturation-to-leading-twist transition remains an active open issue in the CGC precision program.
